chat_notification_https_requirement: All notification types require a trusted HTTPS context. Depending on your browser, a snakeoil certificate may not be sufficient.
chat_notifications_alerts_tab_open: Alerts while this tab is open
chat_notifications_blocked_by_browser: Blocked by browser — check site permissions

chat_analyze_packet_notice: This analyzer shows one stored full packet copy only. When multiple receives have identical payloads, the backend deduplicates them to a single stored packet and appends any additional receive paths onto the message path history instead of storing multiple full packet copies.
chat_archival_packet_purged: The archival raw packet for this message is no longer available. It may have been purged from Settings > Database, so only the stored message and merged route history remain.
chat_bulk_hashtag_description: Paste multiple hashtag channels to add them in one batch
chat_bulk_help_extended: One channel name per line (or comma-separated); spaces are kept as part of the name. Leading # marks are stripped automatically.
chat_bulk_help_normal: Paste channel names separated by lines, spaces, or commas. Leading # marks are stripped automatically.

chat_new_contact_description: Add a new contact by entering their name and public key
chat_no_archival_packet: No archival raw packet is available for this message, so packet analysis cannot be shown.
chat_permit_extended_chars: Permit capitals, whitespace, and extended characters
chat_permit_extended_help_bulk: Off normalizes to lowercase letters, numbers, and dashes. On hashes each name exactly as typed — matches other MeshCore clients and lets you join channels with capitals, spaces, or symbols like &.
chat_permit_extended_help_single: Off normalizes to lowercase letters, numbers, and dashes. On hashes the name exactly as typed — matches other MeshCore clients and lets you join channels with capitals, spaces, or symbols like &.

chat_select_conversation: Select a conversation or start a new one
chat_unknown_full_key_banner: This sender's profile details (name, location) haven't arrived yet. They will fill in automatically when the sender's next advert is heard.
contact_name_only_advert_note: We have not heard an advertisement associated with this name, so we cannot identify their key.
contact_prefix_only_banner: We've received a message from this sender but don't have their full identity yet. This contact stays read-only until their identity is confirmed — this usually happens automatically when they next advertise.
contact_unknown_full_key_banner: This sender's profile details (name, location) haven't arrived yet. They will fill in automatically when the sender's next advertisement is heard.
contact_favorite_ack_hint: Favorite contacts stay loaded on the radio for ACK support
contact_hourly_lines_help: Hourly lines compare the last 24 hours against 7-day and all-time averages for the same hour slots.
contact_name_only_note: Name-only analytics include channel messages only.
contact_attribution_warning_named: Channel sender identity is based on best-effort name matching. Different nodes using the same name will be attributed to the same sender name. Stats below may be inaccurate.
contact_attribution_warning_keyed: Channel sender identity is based on best-effort name matching. Different nodes using the same name will be attributed to the same contact. Stats below may be inaccurate.
contact_attribution_alias_note: Historical counts below may include messages previously attributed under names shown in Also Known As.
contact_no_sensor_data: No sensor data in last response
channel_bulk_review_rooms: Review the newly added rooms below.
channel_ctrl_click_hint: Ctrl+click any room to open it in a new tab.

settings_about_acknowledgements: With great appreciation to those who have made the tools upon which this is built:
settings_push_not_supported: Push notifications are not supported by this browser.
settings_push_requires_https: Web Push requires HTTPS. Access RemoteTerm over HTTPS (self-signed certificates work) to enable push notifications.
settings_push_description_1: Receive notifications even when the browser is closed. Use the bell icon in any conversation header to enable push for that contact or channel, or subscribe this browser to receive notifications for all push-enabled conversations.
settings_push_description_2: The set of channels or DMs that trigger push notifications are global per-install (i.e. all devices that register for Web Push will have the same set of channels/DMs that trigger notifications). Subscribing or unsubscribing a particular browser only controls whether that browser receives notifications for the configured set of channels/DMs.
settings_local_label_description: Display a colored banner at the top of the page to identify this instance.
settings_distance_units_description: Controls how distances are shown throughout the app.
settings_reopen_last_description: Automatically reopen to the last-open channel or contact when the app loads to the bare URL.
settings_auto_focus_description: Place the cursor in the message input when switching conversations. Desktop only.
settings_battery_percent_description: Display the radio's battery percentage in the status bar. Data updates every 60 seconds and may take up to a minute to appear after connecting.
settings_battery_voltage_description: Display the radio's battery voltage in the status bar (in mV). Data updates every 60 seconds and may take up to a minute to appear after connecting.
settings_status_dot_description: Flash the connection status dot in color as packets arrive: blue for channel, purple for DM, cyan for advert, dark green for other.
settings_render_rich_payloads_desc_1: MeshCore Open clients send GIFs and emoji reactions as encoded text (e.g.
settings_render_rich_payloads_desc_3: ). When enabled, these render as the GIF image or reaction emoji instead of the raw text. Reactions show generically (the emoji is not tied to a specific message). GIFs load from media.giphy.com, which reaches outside your local network and exposes your IP to Giphy — so this is off by default.
settings_path_hop_width_desc_1: Append the per-hop identifier width to the hop-count badge on received messages — e.g.
settings_path_hop_width_desc_2: for a 2-hop path with 2-byte hops. Direct (0-hop) messages show no width. Off by default.
settings_text_replace_description: Automatically replace characters as you type in the message input. Define replacements as a JSON object mapping source strings to their replacements.
settings_text_replace_unsaved_suffix: Changes are not saved until this is resolved.
settings_font_size_description: Scales the app's typography for this browser only. The slider moves in 5% steps; the number field accepts any value from 25% to 400%.
settings_local_device_only_note: These settings apply only to this device/browser.
settings_db_delete_undecrypted_desc: Permanently deletes stored raw packets that have not yet been decrypted. These are retained in case you later obtain the correct key — once deleted, these messages can never be recovered.
settings_db_purge_archival_desc: Deletes the raw packet bytes behind messages that are already decrypted and visible in chat. This frees space but removes packet-analysis availability for those messages. It does not affect displayed messages or future decryption.
settings_db_auto_decrypt_label: Auto-decrypt historical DMs when new contact advertises
settings_db_auto_decrypt_desc: When enabled, the server will automatically try to decrypt stored DM packets when a new contact sends an advertisement. This may cause brief delays on large packet backlogs.
settings_db_toast_invalid_retention_desc: Retention days must be at least 1
settings_db_toast_purge_failed_title: Failed to purge decrypted raw packets
settings_meshcomod_cad_supported_desc: Scan for channel activity before each transmit and defer if the channel is busy.
settings_meshcomod_gps_unsupported_desc: This firmware build has no GPS support.
settings_radio_toast_geo_not_supported_d: Your browser does not support geolocation
settings_radio_error_numeric_fields: All numeric fields must have valid values
settings_radio_toast_regions_already_lis: All discovered regions are already listed

settings_radio_toast_regions_added.one: Added {count} region — review and Save Messaging Settings
settings_radio_toast_regions_added.other: Added {count} regions — review and Save Messaging Settings

settings_radio_toast_export_without_key_: See README_ADVANCED.md for private key export enable
settings_radio_toast_invalid_config_desc: File must contain name and radio parameters (freq, bw, sf, cr)
settings_radio_toast_import_with_key: Config + private key imported, saving & rebooting...
settings_radio_toast_connection_change_f: Failed to change radio connection state
settings_radio_toast_check_connection_re: Check radio connection and try again
settings_radio_disconnect_note: Disconnect pauses automatic reconnect attempts so another device can use the radio.
settings_radio_compat_warning_desc: ALL nodes along a message's route — your radio, every repeater, and the recipient — must be running firmware that supports the selected mode. Messages sent with 2-byte or 3-byte hops will be dropped by any node on older firmware.
settings_radio_advert_location_desc: Companion-radio firmware does not distinguish between saved coordinates and live GPS here. When enabled, adverts include the node's current location state. That may be the last coordinates you set from RemoteTerm or live GPS coordinates if the node itself is already updating them. RemoteTerm cannot enable GPS on the node through the interface library.
settings_radio_telemetry_desc: Controls what this radio shares when other nodes request its telemetry. “{deny}” blocks all requests, “{perContact}” uses per-contact permission flags on the radio, and “{allowAll}” shares with any requester.
settings_radio_reboot_note: Some settings may require a reboot to take effect on some radios.
settings_radio_export_import_note: Export saves the current server config to a JSON file. Import loads a config file, applies it, and reboots the radio.
settings_radio_extra_ack_desc: When enabled, the radio sends one extra direct ACK transmission before the normal ACK for received direct messages. This is a firmware-level receive behavior, not a RemoteTerm retry setting.
settings_radio_auto_resend_desc: When enabled, outgoing channel messages that receive no echo within 2 seconds are automatically resent once (byte-perfect, within the 30-second dedup window). Repeaters that already heard the original will ignore the duplicate. This functionality will NOT create double-sent/duplicate messages.
settings_radio_flood_scope_desc: Tag outgoing messages with a region name (e.g. MyRegion). Repeaters configured for that region can forward the traffic, while repeaters configured to deny other regions may drop it. Leave empty to send unscoped (plain flood). Forcing unscoped when a default scope is configured on the radio requires firmware v12 or newer. Individual channels can override this with their own region or an "always unscoped" setting.
settings_radio_known_regions_desc: One region name per line. Incoming region-scoped (TransportFlood/TransportDirect) packets are matched against this list so messages and the packet inspector show a readable region label instead of a raw transport code. Saving a change re-tags existing messages whose original packet is still stored.
settings_radio_discover_regions_desc: Asks nearby repeaters which regions they flood, so you can populate the list above. Uses repeaters from your last mesh discovery sweep when available, otherwise your most recently seen repeaters. Only repeaters in direct range answer, and this only reveals flood-allowed regions (not blocked ones).
settings_radio_max_contacts_desc: Configured radio contact capacity. Favorites reload first, then background maintenance refills to about 80% of this value and offloads once occupancy reaches about 95%.
settings_radio_max_contacts_warning: Your radio reports a hardware limit of {n} contacts. The effective cap will be limited to what the radio supports.
settings_radio_advert_interval_desc: How often to automatically advertise presence. Set to 0 to disable. Minimum: 1 hour. Recommended: 24 hours or higher.
settings_radio_send_advert_desc: Flood adverts propagate through repeaters. Zero-hop adverts are local-only and use less airtime.
settings_radio_mesh_discovery_desc: Discover nearby node types that currently respond to mesh discovery requests: repeaters and sensors.
settings_radio_no_nodes_responded: No supported nodes responded during the last discovery sweep.
settings_radio_heard_here: Heard here: {localSnr} dB SNR / {localRssi} dBm RSSI. Remote heard us: {remoteSnr} dB SNR.
settings_radio_import_key_dialog_desc: This config file contains a private key. Importing it will change your radio's identity — your radio will have a new public key and other nodes will see it as a different device. This cannot be undone without the original key.
settings_radioapp_tracked_repeater_desc: Repeaters opted into automatic telemetry collection are polled on a scheduled interval. To limit mesh traffic, the app caps telemetry at 24 checks per day across all tracked repeaters — so fewer tracked repeaters allows shorter intervals, and more tracked repeaters forces longer ones. Up to {max} repeaters may be tracked at once ({tracked} / {max} slots used).

settings_radioapp_pref_hours.one: Saved preference is {count} hour, but the scheduler is using {effective} hours because
settings_radioapp_pref_hours.other: Saved preference is {count} hours, but the scheduler is using {effective} hours because

settings_radioapp_repeaters_tracked.one: {count} repeater is tracked. Your preference will be restored if you drop back to a supported count.
settings_radioapp_repeaters_tracked.other: {count} repeaters are tracked. Your preference will be restored if you drop back to a supported count.

settings_radioapp_poll_routed_desc: When enabled, tracked repeaters with a direct or routed path (not flood) are polled every hour instead of on the scheduled interval above. Flood-only repeaters still follow the normal schedule.
settings_radioapp_no_tracked_repeaters: No repeaters are being tracked. Enable tracking from a repeater's dashboard.
settings_radioapp_tracked_contact_desc: Non-repeater contacts (companions, rooms, sensors) can also be tracked for periodic LPP telemetry collection (battery, sensors, GPS). Up to 8 contacts may be tracked. The daily check ceiling is shared with tracked repeaters — adding contacts may clamp the interval upward.
settings_radioapp_no_tracked_contacts: No contacts are being tracked. Enable tracking from a contact's info pane.
settings_radioapp_block_discovery_headin: Block Discovery of New Node Types
settings_radioapp_block_discovery_desc: Checked types will be ignored when heard via advertisement. Existing contacts of these types are still updated. This does not affect contacts added manually or via DM.
settings_radioapp_new_types_blocked: New {types} heard via advertisement will not be added to your contact list.
settings_radioapp_blocked_contacts_desc: Blocked contacts are hidden from the sidebar. Blocking only hides messages from the UI — MQTT forwarding and bot responses are not affected. Messages are still stored and will reappear if unblocked.
settings_radioapp_no_blocked_contacts: No blocked contacts. Block contacts from their info pane, viewed by clicking their avatar in any channel, or their name within the top status bar with the conversation open.
settings_radioapp_bulk_delete_desc: Remove multiple contacts or repeaters at once. Useful for cleaning up spam or unwanted nodes. Message history will be preserved.
settings_fanout_desc_mqtt_private: Customizable-scope forwarding of all or some messages to an MQTT broker of your choosing, in raw and/or decrypted form.
settings_fanout_desc_mqtt_ha: Publishes MQTT Discovery payloads so mesh devices appear natively in Home Assistant. Requires HA's built-in MQTT integration connected to the same broker. Select specific contacts for GPS tracking and repeaters for telemetry sensors.
settings_fanout_desc_mqtt_community: MeshcoreToMQTT-compatible raw-packet feed publishing, compatible with community aggregators (in other words, make your companion radio also serve as an observer node). Superset of other Community MQTT presets.
settings_fanout_desc_meshrank: A community MQTT config preconfigured for MeshRank, requiring only the provided topic from your MeshRank configuration. A subset of the primary Community MQTT/meshcoretomqtt configuration; you are free to edit all configuration after creation.
settings_fanout_desc_letsmesh_us: A community MQTT config preconfigured for the LetsMesh US-ingest endpoint, requiring only your email and IATA region code. Good to use with an additional EU configuration for redundancy. A subset of the primary Community MQTT/meshcoretomqtt configuration; you are free to edit all configuration after creation.
settings_fanout_desc_letsmesh_eu: A community MQTT config preconfigured for the LetsMesh EU-ingest endpoint, requiring only your email and IATA region code. Good to use with an additional US configuration for redundancy. A subset of the primary Community MQTT/meshcoretomqtt configuration; you are free to edit all configuration after creation.
settings_fanout_desc_dmc1: A community MQTT config preconfigured for the Dutch MeshCore collector 1 endpoint, requiring only your email and IATA region code. A subset of the primary Community MQTT/meshcoretomqtt configuration; you are free to edit all configuration after creation.
settings_fanout_desc_dmc2: A community MQTT config preconfigured for the Dutch MeshCore collector 2 endpoint, requiring only your email and IATA region code. A subset of the primary Community MQTT/meshcoretomqtt configuration; you are free to edit all configuration after creation.
settings_fanout_desc_meshcore_analyzer_e: A community MQTT config preconfigured for the MeshCore Analyzer EU endpoint (mqtt.meshcore-analyzer.eu), requiring only your email and IATA region code. A subset of the primary Community MQTT/meshcoretomqtt configuration; you are free to edit all configuration after creation.
settings_fanout_desc_webhook: Generic webhook for decrypted channel/DM messages with customizable verb, method, and optional HMAC signature.
settings_fanout_desc_apprise: A wide-ranging generic fanout, capable of forwarding decrypted channel/DM messages to Discord, Telegram, email, SMS, and many others.
settings_fanout_desc_sqs: Send full or scope-customized raw or decrypted packets to an SQS
settings_fanout_desc_bot: A simple, Python-based interface for basic bots that can respond to DM and channel messages.
settings_fanout_desc_map_upload: Upload repeaters and room servers to map.meshcore.io or a compatible map API endpoint.
settings_fanout_no_integration_types: No integration types are currently available.
settings_fanout_mqtt_private_desc: Forward mesh data to your own MQTT broker for home automation, logging, or alerting.
settings_fanout_mqtt_private_plaintext_w: Outgoing messages (DMs and group messages) will be reported to private MQTT brokers in decrypted/plaintext form.
settings_fanout_ha_intro: Publish discovery configs and MeshCore state to your MQTT broker so Home Assistant creates native devices, sensors, GPS trackers, and message events automatically.
settings_fanout_ha_step1_desc: Home Assistant's built-in MQTT integration must point at the same broker configured below.
settings_fanout_ha_step2_desc: Choose repeaters for telemetry sensors and contacts for GPS tracker entities.
settings_fanout_ha_step3_desc: Radio health and message events publish continuously; repeater and contact data update when new data is heard or collected.

settings_fanout_ha_contact_update_desc: — updates passively when advertisements with GPS are heard, and from any GPS reading in the contact's CayenneLPP telemetry. Shown for one contact; a tracker is created for each selected contact.
settings_fanout_ha_entity_lat_lon: — latitude/longitude (plus altitude when telemetry provides it)
settings_fanout_ha_cayennelpp_contact_no: , etc. — CayenneLPP sensors (when the contact is tracked for telemetry; GPS goes to the tracker above)
settings_fanout_ha_message_events_desc: — fires for each message matching the scope below
settings_fanout_ha_entity_trigger_automa: — trigger automations on sender, channel, or message content
settings_fanout_ha_entity_ids_footer_pre: Entity IDs use the first 12 characters of the node's public key. Entities are removed from HA when this integration is disabled or deleted. State topics are published under
settings_fanout_ha_topic_summary_intro: Home Assistant device and entity IDs are keyed off the first 12 characters of each node's public key, not the display name. Those same 12 characters are used in the MQTT state topics below.
settings_fanout_ha_topic_summary_empty: No topic previews available yet. Connect to a radio to resolve the local radio key, and select contacts or repeaters above to preview their published topics.
settings_fanout_ha_discovery_topics_pref: Discovery config topics are also published under
settings_fanout_ha_discovery_topics_suff: , but the topics above are the primary runtime state and event topics.
settings_fanout_ha_gps_tracked_contacts_: in HA, updated whenever an advertisement with GPS coordinates is heard. Useful for tracking mobile nodes on an HA map dashboard.
settings_fanout_ha_telemetry_tracked_rep: Each selected repeater becomes an HA device with sensors for battery voltage, RSSI, SNR, noise floor, packet counts, and uptime. Data updates whenever telemetry is collected (auto-collect runs every ~8 hours, or on manual dashboard fetch). Only repeaters already in the auto-telemetry tracking list appear here (add new repeaters by logging into the repeater and opting in at the bottom of the page).
settings_fanout_ha_no_repeaters_tracked: No repeaters are being auto-tracked for telemetry. Add repeaters to the auto-telemetry tracking list in the Radio section first, then return here to select which ones to expose to HA.
settings_fanout_ha_repeaters_not_found: Auto-tracked repeaters not found in contact list.
settings_fanout_ha_message_events_fire_s: entity in HA with sender, text, channel, and direction attributes. Use HA automations to trigger actions on specific messages, channels, or contacts.
settings_fanout_mqtt_community_desc: Advanced community MQTT editor. Use this for manual meshcoretomqtt-compatible setups or for modifying a saved preset after creation. Only raw RF packets are shared — never decrypted messages.
settings_fanout_websocket_path_hint_suff: for brokers that require a path
settings_fanout_token_audience_hint: Defaults to the broker host when blank
settings_fanout_owner_email_hint: Used to claim your node on the community aggregator

settings_fanout_letsmesh_summary_tail: TLS on, certificate verification on, token audience fixed to
settings_fanout_bot_experimental_desc: This is an alpha feature and introduces automated message sending to your radio; unexpected behavior may occur. Use with caution, and please report any bugs!
settings_fanout_bot_security_warning_des: This feature executes arbitrary Python code on the server. Only run trusted code, and be cautious of arbitrary usage of message parameters.
settings_fanout_bot_dont_wreck_desc: Bots process ALL messages, including their own. Be careful of creating infinite loops!
settings_fanout_bot_define_suffix: function that receives message data and optionally returns a reply.
settings_fanout_bot_available_desc: Standard Python libraries and any modules installed in the server environment.
settings_fanout_bot_note_prefix: Bots respond to all messages, including your own. For channel messages,
settings_fanout_bot_note_suffix: Multiple enabled bots run concurrently. Outgoing messages are serialized with a two-second delay between sends to prevent repeater collision.

settings_fanout_map_dry_run_off_desc: Live uploads are enabled. Each advert is rate-limited to once per hour per node.
settings_fanout_map_dry_run_desc: When enabled, upload payloads are logged at INFO level but not sent. Disable once you have confirmed the logged output looks correct.
settings_fanout_map_api_url_hint_prefix: Leave blank to use the default
settings_fanout_map_enable_geofence_desc: Only upload nodes whose location falls within the configured radius of your radio's own position. Helps exclude nodes with false or spoofed coordinates. Uses the latitude/longitude set in Radio Settings.
settings_fanout_map_no_lat_lon_prefix: Your radio does not currently have a latitude/longitude configured. Geofencing will be silently skipped until coordinates are set in

settings_fanout_map_radius_hint: Nodes further than this distance from your radio's position will not be uploaded.
settings_fanout_over_pill_limit: >{limit} selections made; hiding selection preview to keep the interface clean
settings_fanout_scope_empty_warning: Nothing is selected — this integration will not forward any data.
settings_fanout_scope_hint_only: Newly added channels or contacts will not be automatically included.
settings_fanout_scope_hint_except: Newly added channels or contacts will be automatically included unless excluded here.
settings_fanout_apprise_intro_middle: when messages are received. Supports Discord, Slack, Telegram, email, and
settings_fanout_apprise_urls_hint_prefix: One URL per line. All URLs receive every matched notification. For Matrix room version 12 (servername-less room IDs), append
settings_fanout_apprise_preserve_identit: When enabled, Discord webhooks will use their configured name/avatar instead of overriding with MeshCore sender info.
settings_fanout_apprise_forward_outgoing: Include DMs and channel messages sent by this RemoteTerm instance, including manual sends and bot replies. Outgoing messages carry no routing path or signal data, so path-related format fields render as direct and RSSI/SNR are empty.
settings_fanout_apprise_markdown_formatt: If notifications fail on services like Telegram due to special characters in sender names, disable this option.
settings_fanout_apprise_var_hops_backtic: Hops wrapped in backticks for markdown
settings_fanout_apprise_empty_textareas_: Empty textareas use the default format. RSSI/SNR may be empty if unavailable.
settings_fanout_webhook_desc: Send message data as JSON to an HTTP endpoint when messages are received.

settings_fanout_sqs_desc: Send matched mesh events to an Amazon SQS queue for durable processing by workers, Lambdas, or downstream automation.
settings_fanout_sqs_plaintext_warning: Outgoing messages and any selected raw packets will be delivered exactly as forwarded by the fanout scope, including decrypted/plaintext message content.
settings_fanout_sqs_endpoint_hint: Useful for LocalStack or custom endpoints
settings_fanout_sqs_static_credentials_d: Leave blank to use the server's normal AWS credential chain.
settings_fanout_error_missing_config_id: Missing fanout config id for update
settings_fanout_experimental_beta_notice: Integrations are an experimental feature in open beta, and allow you to fanout raw and decrypted messages across multiple services for automation, analysis, or archiving.
settings_fanout_bots_disabled_until_rest: Bot system is disabled until the server restarts. Bot integrations cannot run, be created, or be modified right now.
settings_fanout_bots_disabled_by_config: Bot system is disabled by server configuration (MESHCORE_DISABLE_BOTS). Bot integrations cannot run, be created, or be modified.
settings_fanout_error_dialog_desc: Most recent backend error retained for this integration.
settings_statistics_loading: Loading statistics... this can take a while if you have a lot of stored packets.
settings_statistics_path_hash_parsed: Parsed stored raw packets from the last 24 hours: {count}
settings_statistics_noise_floor_samples_: Samples are collected every minute and retained until server restart.
settings_statistics_noise_floor_no_sampl: No noise floor samples collected yet. {note}
settings_statistics_noise_floor_one_samp: Only one sample so far ({dbm} dBm). More data needed for a chart. {note}
